HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a graph-based algorithm known for its excellent recall and speed tradeoff, achieving O(log N) query time. It typically provides 95-99% recall at 10 nearest neighbors with a latency of about 1 millisecond for 1 million vectors. However, it has high memory usage, with parameters such as M (connections) typically set between 16-32, and ef (query) starting at 50-100 for tuning recall performance. HNSW is implemented in various systems like FAISS, Qdrant, and Weaviate. [1][2][3]

IVF (Inverted File) is a cluster-based algorithm that probes the nearest clusters, making it more memory-efficient compared to HNSW. It is particularly suitable for large-scale datasets, allowing for a significant reduction in memory usage, with vector sizes ranging from 64-256 bytes compared to 4KB for float32 1024-dimensional vectors. IVF can be combined with Product Quantization (PQ) to further enhance memory efficiency, although this may result in some loss of recall. [2][3]
